subject.title: [Bug]: MidTurnPrecheckSignal leaks error to UI via pushLoopFailure before internal retry completes

question: Should this be fixed by accepting a generic agent-core control-flow error contract, or by keeping `MidTurnPrecheckSignal` handling entirely inside the embedded-runner recovery boundary?
rationale: The bug is source-provable, but the durable fix sets an owner boundary between reusable agent-core failure streaming and OpenClaw-specific mid-turn recovery.

options.title: Finish the focused agent-core seam
options.body: Accept the generic `agent-core.controlFlowError` direction from the linked PR after live retry proof and lifecycle/session-state review.

options.title: Move handling into embedded runner
options.body: Keep agent-core unaware of this signal and catch or prevent the control-flow error before it reaches generic failure streaming.

options.title: Wait for broader compaction work
options.body: Pause this issue on the broader mid-turn precheck compaction PR, accepting a longer path and more review surface.

recommendation.title: Finish the focused agent-core seam
recommendation.body: Accept the generic `agent-core.controlFlowError` direction from the linked PR after live retry proof and lifecycle/session-state review.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the mid-turn precheck feature and own the broader overlapping precheck compaction PR, so they are the best routing candidate for the boundary decision.
